report.summary: The proposal to restore a status is directionally right but must be narrowed before it is safe. A pure restoration step would conflict with the existing status-adjustment record in three concrete ways. (1) lib/delivery-assessment.ts:533-535 adds every status change to the publication's adjustedCriteria ledger. For scenario A, a restoration would create an adjustedCriteria entry (insufficient_evidence -> changes_suggested) under reason "item_status_adjusted". lib/evidence-export.ts:271 and :252 accept that shape, so the export check passes. However, the independent replay at :347-350 recomputes sourceFinding as changes_suggested, so the report is internally contradictory: the published item says insufficient_evidence, yet its retained original changes_suggested is not reproduced. This is the same pub7/9 vs source-effective9/9 gap shifted from the live report to the export. (2) For scenario B, restoration would replace the catalog fact-citation bound at 8 (assessment-source-findings.ts:47) with the published cap of at most 6 (proposed). That budget can legitimately return insufficient_evidence even when sourceFinding is changes_suggested, so a restore keyed only on sourceFinding.status would override a deliberate evidence-budget guard. (3) The proposal says that the raw insufficient_evidence status must be preserved on the modelJudgment field (lib/delivery-assessment.ts:293). lib/evidence-export.ts:352 requires each adjustedCriteria originalStatus to equal modelJudgment.status, but publishSourceAssessmentNotes receives only published statuses (lib/assessment-publication-policy.ts:108-112). Unless the new schema or provenance work reconciles the two, the export's ai-source-citations check will fail with an inconsistent export. Fixes should be a server-recomputed, criterion-scoped reconciliation record; preserving the raw status is necessary but is not by itself sufficient.

findings.title: A status restored to changes_suggested after publication diverges from the independent sourceFinding replay, producing an internally contradictory or unexportable report
findings.evidence: Line 535 passes `items` (possibly restored) and `originalStatuses` into publishSourceAssessmentNotes. That function records any difference in adjustedCriteria (assessment-publication-policy.ts:111) and publishes with withheldRisks.version 1 reason "item_status_adjusted" (line 118-120). evidence-export.ts:271 accepts that version 1 whenever adjustedCriteria.length > 0. At :347-350 the export recomputes checkSource(...). For scenario A, prices.kind === "mismatch" (source-business-evidence.ts:169; assessment-source-findings.ts:48), so expected is changes_suggested even when the published item status is a restored changes_suggested. If the restore is implemented as status = sourceFinding.status without a separate ledger entry, the restored item merely moves the same mismatch that the proposal removes: the published item still says insufficient_evidence while sourceFinding says changes_suggested. Under the existing policy the withheldRisks entry type is derived only from published statuses. There is no place where the model's raw status, the published status, and the sourceFinding status are all recorded together, so an export verifier cannot tell an independent-source restoration apart from an ordinary adjustment.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace. Scenario A: a restored item has modelJudgment.status=changes_suggested, published status=changes_suggested, sourceFinding.status=changes_suggested with basis=locked_business_values and citations for the AUD 28 block. publishSourceAssessmentNotes(..., originalStatuses=changes_suggested) sees no change, so statusAdjustedCount=0. That either (a) keeps the export at version 1 "not_withheld" and contradicts the proposal's stated prior-7/9 change, or (b) if any other item was adjusted, the ledger says the AUD 28 item's originalStatus=changes_suggested and publishedStatus=changes_suggested. That fails the :255 requirement that originalStatus !== publishedStatus, or the :110 status transition check. If instead the raw insuff was published, sourceFinding=changes_suggested conflicts with status=insufficient_evidence and has no ledger annotation that :350's replay can distinguish.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit, criterion-scoped reconciliation annotation that is recomputed on the server. It should record rawModelStatus, publishedStatus, and sourceFinding status/basis plus the effective scopeBinding. Publish it only when the same-criterion replay equals changes_suggested and the citations are exact. Extend assessment() (evidence-export.ts:192) and the adjustedCriteria checks (:251-256) to validate that annotation, rather than reusing the version 1 item_status_adjusted ledger for restorations.

findings.title: The sourceFinding citation cap (8) is looser than the proposed published cap (6), so restoring on sourceFinding.status can override an intentional citation-budget insufficient_evidence result
findings.evidence: Line 47 lets sourceFinding be changes_suggested with up to 8 citations. The published-item paths use ASSESSMENT_ITEM_CITATION_LIMIT (6) in the presence and label guards (lib/assessment-evidence-scope.ts paths and lib/delivery-assessment.ts:463). The proposed restore condition is only 'nonempty exact fact citations <= existing 6 cap'. That wording does not require the same citations to be the ones whose count drove the guard to the 8-vs-6 grey zone. For a locked_business_values criterion with 7-8 distinct fact citations, sourceFinding=changes_suggested and the published computed=insufficient_evidence would satisfy the condition, so the restore re-relaxes a server-derived budget guard.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning. Construct a criterion with 7 business checks whose citation spans are distinct; prices.kind=mismatch yields 7 unique citations, so assessment-source-findings.ts:46-48 returns changes_suggested. The published items[].citations slot can hold only 6, and the guard that produced insufficient_evidence was the citation-budget path. A threshold-only check (<=6 nonempty exact citations) would silently keep a subset of 6 and publish changes_suggested, treating a value the server deliberately withheld as needing per-check inspection as publishable under a cite subset.
findings.suggestion: Require that the restored citations are exactly the sourceFinding citations filtered for the same criterion, or require that the restored set equals the full fact set and is <= 6, not merely 'a nonempty subset <= 6'. If the full fact set exceeds 6, keep insufficient_evidence.

findings.title: The published status cannot be inferred from sourceFinding alone, so any restored item must also satisfy the adjustedCriteria originalStatus === modelJudgment.status check
findings.evidence: Line 352 requires `adjustment.originalStatus === item.modelJudgment?.status` for every item that has a withheldRisks.adjustedCriteria entry. The proposal keeps raw modelJudgment unchanged (delivery-assessment.ts:293). The withheldRisks is built in assessment-publication-policy.ts:108-120 from originalStatuses = raw statuses and item.status = possibly restored statuses. If a restored item's raw status is not the status passed as originalStatus, the export fails with 'the retained original AI status conflicts with its adjustment ledger'. That turns scenario A/B into an unexportable report, a regression from today's exportable pub7/9 record, unless the new provenance and reconciliation schema is designed with this check in mind.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace. Suppose the restored item has modelJudgment.status=insufficient_evidence (raw), item.status=changes_suggested (restored), and an entry in withheldRisks.adjustedCriteria with originalStatus=... If originalStatus is taken from the raw model status, :352 passes (insufficient_evidence === insufficient_evidence). That is feasible only if the version 1 ledger is treated as legitimate for restorations too, which conflicts with the finding above (a policy adjustment is then indistinguishable from an independent-source restoration). If originalStatus is taken from the pre-publication computed status (insufficient_evidence too), the modelJudgment mismatch is avoided, but the raw-vs-published distinction is still lost.
findings.suggestion: Make the restoration record a first-class, server-recomputed field (for example rawStatus, publishedStatus, sourceFinding status/basis, citing the same-criterion replay equality). Validate it in assessment() and in :350-352 so the export can recompute the bounded reconciliation rather than relying on the generic adjustedCriteria ledger.

findings.title: Independent per-criterion facts are already available; the restore must be scoped, not global, so the model's known legacy checker false verdicts are not reintroduced for business-check criteria
findings.evidence: Lines 494-503 apply labelSourceFactsCheck only when the criterion has no saved business steps. independentSourceCheck is computed per criterion (:506) and returns insufficient_evidence when prices.kind is unknown (assessment-source-findings.ts:48). Scenario A's legacy checker reports unknown(dynamic_or_unsupported_source) for that criterion (source-business-evidence.ts:148). A restore keyed on raw status alone, without the required sourceFinding=changes_suggested and exact citations, could mark that AU28 item as changes_suggested using the very business path the labels intentionally exclude from the label facts. Limiting restores to the two named families (locked_business_values mismatch and declared_html_labels with scopeBinding) avoids that, but the proposal does not say how the criterion family is identified.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning. If the restore condition is implemented at line 506 as 'if raw==insufficient_evidence&&sourceFinding?.status==="changes_suggested"', the criterion is the business-check item. sourceFinding is changes_suggested precisely because the independent price fact check found a mismatch. That is the desired outcome for A. But any unrelated criterion whose raw is insufficient_evidence and whose sourceFinding is also changes_suggested (from a shared mis-parsed price) would be restored too, even if its guard failed for a different reason (dynamic source, ambiguity). The proposal does not bound which insufficient_evidence reasons can be restored.
findings.suggestion: Gate the restore on the specific guard that produced insufficient_evidence (for example the business unknown path, or the label citation-adjustment no_complete_group path). Do not gate only on sourceFinding.status. Also record basis and scopeBinding in the reconciliation record so restorations remain auditable per criterion.

limitations: Read-only design review of the supplied packet only. No files were changed and no code was run. All reproductions are source-reading reasoning traces labeled unexecuted; no typecheck, tests, provider replay, or export verification was executed.

Several referenced modules are not included in the packet and could not be verified: contracts.ts (ProofAssessmentSourceFinding, ProofAssessmentItem, withheldRisks types), assessment-evidence-needs.ts, assessment-limits.ts (the value of ASSESSMENT_ITEM_CITATION_LIMIT), source-presence-evidence.ts, exact-copy-evidence.ts, positive-literal-source-witness.ts, universal-tag-evidence.ts, universal-source-list-evidence.ts, scope-clarifications.ts, native-form-source.ts, source-literal-directive.ts, and assessment-obligations.ts. The assertions about the 6-citation cap rely on the proposal's own statement plus the constant references, not on the constant's definition.

The claimed actual residual scenarios A and B (specific AUD 28 menu render, the contact.html#contact versus index.html#other records) and the prior 7/9 versus source-effective 9/9 counts could not be reproduced from the packet. No saved quote, report, or model output was supplied, so those counts remain unverified claims.

The export path (evidence-export.ts:335-356) filters files to html/css (line 347) and recomputes sourceFinding from exact bytes. Any proposed new report provenance field must survive that filter and recomputation; the precise field shape is not in the packet and could not be designed or validated here.

It is taken only as the prompt's stated verification and no competitor score or capability assertion is made. No current-cycle champion-protocol record was reviewed.

The proposal's prohibition (no general semantic engine, no new auth or adapter, no retrying the four real calls) and its acceptance of the existing conservative default guard were treated as fixed constraints and are not re-litigated. No Devpost, video, submission, or deployment claim is made.
